question: A 4-month-old, on breastfeeding, is brought to the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illness (IMNCI) clinic by her mother with signs of pneumonia. What will be the most appropriate advice given to the mother for the prevention of low blood sugar?

answers.option: Give sugar and water solution 2 hourly

question: A 2-day-old male infant is brought to the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) with the complaint of jaundice since birth. The baby was born full-term normal vaginal delivery at a hospital. There is a history of prolonged rupture of membranes. On examination, the baby is sick-looking, with moderate anemia and deep jaundice (up to sole). Heart rate is 170 beats/min, respiratory rate is 78 breaths/min, and temperature is 101 °F. Further examination reveals poor reflexes and an absence of visceromegaly. Investigations: Hb 9 g/dL, WBC 25000/mm^3 (N: 65%, L: 25%), platelets 150000/mm^3, reticulocytes 10%, total bilirubin 28 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 2 mg/dL. Urine is positive for hemoglobin. What will be the next appropriate investigation for this infant?

A 7-year-old child is brought to the emergency room by his parents with complaints of increasing paleness of the body and no passage of urine since the morning. The parents give the history of bloody diarrhea 5 days back. On examination, the child is found to be irritable and moderately anemic signs. His complete blood picture (CBC) shows hemoglobin 6 mg/dl, total leukocyte count (TLC) 13000 cells/cubic millimeter of blood, and platelet 75000 platelets per microliter of blood. What is the child most likely suffering from?

A 7-year-old child, who was previously diagnosed with asthma, is brought to the outpatient department with on and off cough for the past two months. He had day-time symptoms twice in the last month, but no night-time symptoms. What is the most appropriate treatment?
An 8-month-old male baby is brought to the clinic with his parents asking for the deworming of the child. According to IMNCI, what is the most appropriate plan?

answers.option: Mebendazole every six months from the age of 1 year
Pyrantel pamoate every six months from the age of 1 month
Pyrantel pamoate every three months from the age of 6 months
Albendazole every three months from the age of 6 months
Mebendazole every three months from the age of 6 months

question: A 7-year-old female is brought to the emergency room due to a history of arthralgia, and jaundice for the past two months. She is also known to have anorexia. Her viral markers are found to be negative. The doctor suspects a diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis type 2. Which antibody test can be done to confirm the doctor's suspicion?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to the emergency room by his parents with a complaint of abdominal pain for the past few days. On examination, rashes are found on his legs and buttocks. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-week-old baby is referred to neonatal ICU (NICU) for the examination of murmur. On examination, the baby appeared in his usual state but a thrill and a 4/6 grade murmur are heard at the left lower sternal border. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-month-old boy is brought to the outpatient department with a complaint of diarrhea for the past 2 months. The mother adds that stools are watery in nature. The baby is on breastfeed and formula milk. On examination, there is a diaper rash and milk dehydration. The stool DR shows pH = 5, occasional pus cells, and no red blood cells. What is the most appropriate investigation?

A 6-month-old child is brought to the outpatient department with complaints of not gaining weight and being reluctant to feed. On examination, the baby's heart rate is 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate 55 breaths per minute, and has a machinery murmur at the left upper sternal border with bounding pulse and wide pulse pressure. What is the best treatment option?

A 4-year-old farmer's boy is brought to the emergency department with a complaint of an altered state of consciousness for the past one hour. On examination, the boy is found to be excessively salivating and has pinpoint pupils. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old is brought to the outpatient department by his parents with a complaint of diarrhea for the past 1 to 2 months. His mother also complaints of passing the stool 3 to 4 times a day and having undigested food particles. On examination, the child weighs 14.5 kg, height is 96 cm and shows no signs of dehydration. Stool DR shows pH = 7, 3-4 pus cells, and no presence of red blood cells. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child, a known case of asthma, takes a steroid inhaler in low doses with good technique but his symptoms are not controlled and hinder his daily activities. What is the most appropriate next step?

answers.option: Increase the dose of inhaled steriod

question: A 2-year-old is brought to the emergency room with a complaint of paleness. His mother further states that the child has a poor diet. On examination, the child shows anemic signs with no visceromegaly. What is the most likely laboratory finding in this child to make a diagnosis?

answers.option: Low red blood cell distribution width

question: An 8-month-old infant, born prematurely, is brought to the clinic for immunization. He weighs 5 Kg and looks pale and irritable. His systemic examination is unremarkable. A blood complete picture shows hemoglobin = 4.3 mg%, TLC = 8700/mm^3, lymphocytes = 45%, neutrophils = 50%, eosinophils = 2%, monocytes = 3%, MCV = 60 fL, MCHC = 24 g/dL, MCH = 21 pg, and serum transferrin saturation < 15%. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old girl presents with difficulty breathing, following an acute episode of severe, watery diarrhea and vomiting. On examination, she is in severe dehydration with deep and rapid breathing. Her chest is clear. Blood pressure is 130/80 mmHg. An arterial blood gas analysis reveals pH 7.00, pCO2 15 mm/Hg, pO2 95 mm/Hg, and HCO3 10 mEq/L. What is the most appropriate investigation to confirm the diagnosis?

An 8-month-old baby born prematurely at the gestational age of 36 weeks now comes to the clinic for a routine check-up. The baby looks pale, is easily irritable, and weighs around 5.5 kilograms. A complete blood count is ordered which shows a total leucocyte count (TLC) 0f 8700/microlitres (lymphocytes = 45%, neutrophils = 50%, others = 2%), hemoglobin 4.3 g/L, mean corpuscular volume (MCV) 60 fL, mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH) 21 pg/cell, and mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC) 24 % Hb/cell. Serum transferrin saturation is found to be less than 15%. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-day-old infant comes to the clinic with the complaint of bilious vomiting since birth. There is no associated abdominal distention. The mother reveals that she had polyhydramnios during the pregnancy. An abdominal X-ray is ordered which shows a double bubble gas shadow. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child is brought by his mother to the outpatient department with the complaint that he has sudden episodes of a blank look on his face lasting for a few seconds. She further adds that the episodes have increased in frequency over the past few weeks. Which of the following drugs is the most appropriate for this condition?

A 7-year-old child who is a known case of asthma is brought by his parents to the clinic with complaints of on and off cough for the past 2 months. On inquiry, the parents reveal that he had 2 episodes of daytime attacks during the last month and no nighttime symptoms. Which of the following would be the most appropriate treatment?

A 2-day-old baby born via normal vaginal delivery now presents with respiratory distress and central cyanosis. On auscultation, a single S2 heart sound is heard. No murmurs are appreciated. Which of the following would be the most likely diagnosis?

A 10-year-old unimmunized child weighing 30 Kg, belonging to a poor socio-economic group, and a resident of urban slums presents to the outpatient department with complaints of high-grade continuous fever for 10 days. On examination, the patient has a toxic look, his tongue is coated, and the spleen is palpable 3 cm below the costal margin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old male child is brought by his parents with a history of loose stools for 3 days. On examination, the child is lethargic and is unable to drink water. How will you manage the child according to the Integrated management of newborn and childhood illness (IMNCI)?

answers.option: Ora; rehydration solution 75 mL/Kg in 4 hours
Intravenous ringer's lactate 100 mL/Kg in 3 hours

question: A 3-year-old child is brought by his parents with a history of loose stools for 2 days. There is no history of blood in stool, On examination, the child is irritable and thirsty. How can this child be classified according to the integrated management of newborn and childhood illness (IMNCI)?

A one-and-a-half-month-old child presents to the clinic with a complaint of a rash over the scalp and neck. On examination, he has a scaly, greasy, papular rash over the scalp and neck. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-day-old premature infant weighing 2 kg is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of respiratory distress since birth. On examination, his chest is deflated, air entry is reduced on both sides of the lungs, and cyanosis is present. Chest X-ray shows ground glass appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old who is a known case of diabetes is brought by his parents to the emergency department with a complaint of respiratory distress. Arterial blood gases show pH = 7.00, pCO2 = 30 mmHg, pO2 = 115 mmHg, and a concentration of HCO3 is 15 mmol/L. His random blood sugar (RBS) is 416 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely metabolic abnormality?
A child presents to the clinic to seek medical advice. The child is lacking clean clothing and has poor personal hygiene. Which of the following conditions has these signs?

A mother brings her 1-month-old baby to the outpatient department with a complaint of persistent vomiting for the last week. The vomiting is projectile and non-bilious. On examination, the child is irritable and hungry. An oval-shaped mass is palpable in the epigastric region. Which of the following is the initial investigation of choice to reach the diagnosis?

An 8-day-old female child presents to the outpatient department with complaints of poor feeding and jaundice. The baby is on formula feed. On examination, the baby is lethargic and has a central cataract. Her random blood sugar levels are in the hypoglycemic range. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
Expanded Programme on Immunisation (EPI) contains a killed vaccine. Which of the following diseases is prevented by that vaccine?

A 5-day-old male weighing 3 Kg presents to the clinic with the complaint of jaundice since birth. On examination, the baby is anemic and the spleen is enlarged 2 cm below the costal margin. On investigation, it is found that the blood groups of the baby and the mother are B negative and A positive respectively, and an increased reticulocyte count. Liver function tests show total serum bilirubin of 21 mg/dL and direct serum bilirubin of 2 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Neonatal jaundice due to breast milk jaundice
Neonatal jaundice due to glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency
Neonatal jaundice due to congenital hypothyroidism
Neonatal jaundice due to ABO incompatibility
Neonatal jaundice due to Rh incompatibility

question: A 10-year-old fully immunized male child weighing 30 kg presents to the emergency department with complaints of cough, shortness of breath, and tachypnea. On examination, flaring of nostrils, intercostal and suprasternal retractions, hyperinflation, and a hyper-resonant chest are noted. On auscultation, bilateral rhonchi are audible. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of recurrent episodes of epistaxis and gum bleeding since he was 2 years of age. He is a product of nonconsanguineous marriage with no family history of bleeding disorders. On examination, he is a young healthy boy of good height and weight. There are a few bruises over his arm and there is blood staining his gums. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the first investigation that needs to be ordered for reaching a diagnosis?

answers.option: Partial thromboplastin time (PTT) and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT)

question: An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of two episodes of hematemesis since morning. On examination, he is pale, anxious, afebrile, and mildly jaundiced. Abdominal examination shows a distended abdomen with prominent veins, positive shifting dullness, and an enlarged spleen 6 cm below the costal margin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-month-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of fever and runny nose for 2 days. The child now has difficulty in breathing and is reluctant to feed since morning. On examination, the temperature is 38°C (100.4°F), the heart rate is 190 beats per minute, and the respiratory rate is 60 breaths per minute. Chest auscultation reveals fine crepitations. Capillary refill time is 2 seconds and the liver is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin. What is the most appropriate treatment to be given to this patient ?

An 8-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a history of fever for 5 days, a single episode of fits, and an altered state of consciousness since morning. On examination, his GCS is 7/15, signs of meningeal irritation are positive, and there is a purpuric rash present on the legs and buttocks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old female comes to the outpatient department with a history of deterioration of school performance and abnormal jerky movements for the last two months. On examination, there is dystonia and Kayser-Fleischer rings in the eyes. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old female presents to the clinic with complaints of fever, headache, and vomiting. The patient also gives a history of ear discharge for more than a week for which she took antibiotics. On examination, there is left-sided weakness and up-going planters on the left. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with complaints of difficulty breathing, fever, and chest pain for 10 days. On examination, the temperature is 38.3°C (101°F), the respiratory rate is 42 minutes per minute, and the heart rate is 102 beats per minute. Respiratory examination reveals a stony dull percussion note and decreased breath sounds on the right side of the chest. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 18-month-old boy comes to the clinic with complaints of fever, cough, and hoarseness of voice for 2 days. On examination, the temperature is 102°F (38.89°C
), the heart rate is 100 beats per minute and, the respiratory rate is 55 breaths per minute. There is an inspiratory stridor present. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

An 8-year-old female is brought to the emergency department with complaints of generalized body swelling and decrease urine output for 2 days. Past medical history reveals episode of joint swelling and malar rash few weeks back. On examination, blood pressure is 120/90 mmHg. Laboratory investigations reveal protienuria +3, RBC 10-15/HPF, WBC 4-5/HPF. Anti-nuclear antobodies and anti-double stranded DNA antibodies are positive. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old child presents to the outpatient department with the complaint of not being able to communicate socially and verbally, have no friends, and involves in solitary repetitive play for hours. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-day-old female presents to the clinic with respiratory distress, grunting, and cyanosis. On examination, there is bilateral decreased air entry and a scaphoid-shaped abdomen. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old male presents to the clinic with the complaint of multiple dark spots on the whole body. The spots are 6-10 mm, variable in diameter. Axillary freckling and numerous small nodules are also noticed on the skin. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A newborn female infant presents to the clinic with the complaint of cyanosis on rest and feeding. The cyanosis improves when the baby cries. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-month-old boy presents to the clinic with the complaint of persistent vomiting since birth. He is severely dehydrated. On systemic examination, external genitals are normal. Laboratory investigations show normal blood count, serum Na of 126 mEq/L, serum K of 5.6 mEq/L, and random blood sugar of 40 mg/dL. Arterial blood gases show a pH of 7.3, and a concentration of HCO3 10 mEq/L. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child comes to the clinic with complaints of short stature. On further investigation, it is found that his bone age is 6 years old while his height age is 4 years old. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 1-year-old baby is brought to the clinic with complaints of frequent watery stools. The baby is bottle-fed. On examination, he is lethargic and floppy. His eyes are sunken and have absent tears. How will you classify the hydration status of this child?

A neonate born after a difficult delivery has gasping respiration and his heart rate is 70 beats per minute. The resuscitation team starts resuscitative efforts and even after 30 seconds of positive pressure ventilation, the respiration fails to improve. Which of the following is the next best step in the management of this child?

A 3-year-old child presents to the clinic with a complaint of watery stools for 1 day. On examination, the child is mildly dehydrated, irritable, and restless, and his abdominal skin feels doughy. His blood pressure and urine output are within normal limits. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A developmentally normal child, who is just able to sit without support, transfers object from hand to hand and speaks in monosyllabic babble. What is the age of the child at this point?

A 4-month-old breastfed baby is brought to the IMNCI clinic and classified as having pneumonia. Which of the following is the most appropriate advice given to the mother to prevent low blood sugar in the child?

A full-term male infant weighing 4.5 Kg is just born via an assisted delivery to an unbooked mother. The baby cries immediately but looks plethoric. Which of the following is the most appropriate investigation to be performed immediately?

answers.option: Blood sugar of the mother and the baby
Blood sugar and calcium of the baby

question: A 7-year-old child is brought to the emergency department with complaints of increasing pallor and anuria since morning. There is a history of bloody diarrhea 5 days back. On examination, the child is irritable and moderately anemic. Complete blood count shows Hb of 6 gm/dL, total leucocyte count of 13000/mm3, and platelet count of 75000/mm3. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A baby born in a private hospital by a lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) develops tachypnea within 6 hours after birth. A respiratory examination shows sub-costal retraction and cyanosis. Chest X-ray reveals prominent pulmonary vascular markings and fluid in the interlobar fissure. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of fever and right knee joint swelling. There is a history of similar complaints in the left ankle joint 5 days back and a rash. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 7-year-old child who is a known case of asthma comes to the clinic for a regular follow-up visit. The child is on low-dose inhaled steroids, he uses the inhaler with the appropriate technique and is compliant. His symptoms are uncontrolled along with the limitation of daily activities. Which of the following will be the most appropriate next step to gain control?

answers.option: Increase the dose of inhaled steroid

question: A 7-year-old female child presents to the emergency department with a history of anorexia, arthralgia, and jaundice for two months. His viral markers are all negative. The doctor suspects immune hepatitis type B. Which of the following is the diagnostic antibody for the confirmation of immune hepatitis type B?

answers.option: Auto antibody against soluble liver antigen

question: A 7-year-old child presents to the emergency department with a history of passing cola-colored urine since morning and severe headache for 2 hours. The patient gives a history of skin infection 15 days back treated by a local general practitioner. Which of the following is the most important vital sign to be examined in this child?
A 7-year-old girl is receiving anti-tuberculous therapy and presents to the clinic with complaints of impaired color vision. Which of the following drugs is the most likely cause of this complaint?

A 7-day-old baby is brought to the emergency department with complaints of cyanosis since the second day of birth. On examination, he has an ejection systolic murmur at the left upper sternal border. Chest  X-ray shows an egg on string appearance. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

answers.option: Transposition of great vessels with atrial septal defect

question: A 6-year-old male child presents to the clinic with a history of abdominal pain. On examination, he has rashes over his legs and buttocks. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A 7-month-old baby is brought to the clinic with the complaint of failure to thrive. He is on goat milk feed. Which of the following laboratory parameters will be elevated in this patient?

A 6-year-old child presents to the clinic with an X-ray that shows lytic bone lesions in the skull and pelvis. He is also reported to be passing frequent dilute urine. On examination, he has scaly, papular skin rashes around the body and generalized lymphadenopathy. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of polyuria and polydipsia for the last 6 months after trauma from falling off a bicycle. Which of the following is the child most likely suffering from?

A 6-month-old child comes to the clinic for routine immunization. The mother is concerned about the possible side effects of the rotavirus vaccine. Which of the following is a possible complication of the said vaccine?

A 6-week-old baby is referred to the neonatal ICU with a murmur on examination. On further examination, the baby is well but there is a thrill and grade 4/6 murmur heard over the left lower sternal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old boy presents to the clinic with a history of swelling of elbows, knees, and ankles for 2 months. The joint swelling is associated with morning stiffness in the joints. He has been taking ibuprofen for 1 week, but there is no improvement. Which of the following is the most important treatment for this child?

A 2-day-old infant presents to the neonatal ICU with the complaint of jaundice since birth. The baby was born at term via normal vaginal delivery with a history of prolonged rupture of membranes. On examination, the baby is looking sick with moderate anemia and deep jaundice up to the soles. His heart rate is 170 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 70 breaths per minute, and temperature is 101°F (38.3°C). There is no visceromegaly and the reflexes are poor. A complete blood count shows a hemoglobin of 9 mg/dL, and a WBC count of 25000 per microlitre ( Lymphocytes = 25%, neutrophils = 65%). The reticulocyte count is 10% and liver function tests show a total bilirubin of 28 mg/dL and direct bilirubin of 2 mg/dL. Urine is positive for hemoglobin. Which of the following is the next best step in the investigations of this child?

A 5-year-old child presents to the clinic with a history of difficulty in climbing stairs. On examination, there is hypertrophy of the calf muscles. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-month-old child presents to the clinic with complaints of inability to gain weight and reluctance to feed. On examination, the heart rate is 120 beats per minute and the respiratory rate is 55 breaths per minute. Cardiovascular examination reveals a machinery-like murmur at the left upper sternal border with bounding pulses and wide pulse pressure. Which of the following is the best treatment option?

A 5-year-old male child presents to the clinic with complaints of swelling and pain in both ankle and knee joints for two weeks. There is no history of any associated fever. On examination, the joints are swollen and tender with mild restriction of movements. There are two bruises on the left arm and one on the back. There is no history of bleeding at the time of circumcision. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-day-old neonate is brought to the neonatal ICU with complaints of not taking feeds and fits for the last two days. The baby was delivered at home. On examination, the temperature is 101°F (38.3°C), the body is rigid on touch and there is an inability to open the mouth. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old baby comes to the emergency department with the complaint of a weak cry. On examination, the baby is hypotonic with an umbilical hernia. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old female child presents to the clinic with a complaint of nasal bleeding for 2 days. On examination, she is afebrile and her vitals are stable. There are petechial rashes all over her body. Her chest and central nervous system examinations are normal, there is no hepatosplenomegaly on abdominal examination. A complete blood count shows Hemoglobin of 11 gm/dL and a total leucocyte count of 7200/mm3 (Neutrophils = 63%, lymphocytes = 35%, eosinophils = 2%). Platelet count is 197000/mm3, activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) is 90 seconds, and prothrombin time (PT) is 13 seconds. Bleeding time is prolonged. Which of the following tests will you advise to reach a diagnosis?

A 4-year-old farmer boy is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of an altered state of consciousness for 1 hour. On examination, there is excessive salivation with pinpoint pupils. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 5-year-old boy who is a known case of asthma is brought to the emergency department with the complaint of difficulty in breathing for 1 day. On examination, the respiratory rate is 60 breaths per minute, the heart rate is 100 beats per minute, the temperature is 98.6°F (37°C) and the oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. Chest auscultation reveals bilateral wheeze. What is the immediate management of thus condition?

A 5-day-old baby is brought to the clinic with the complaint of swelling on the scalp. On examination, the child is pale looking with the swelling fluctuating and extending over the eyes and ears. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old active playful boy is brought to the clinic with a history of red spots over the skin for a few days.  On examination, the vital signs are normal and there are numerous petechiae present over the trunk and extremities. The rest of the systemic and general physical examination is normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 4-year-old boy is brought to the outpatient department with the complaint of red-colored urine for one day.  A urine dipstick test is done that is negative for heme. Which of the following is the cause of red urine in this patient?

A 3-year-old girl presents to the outpatient department with the complaint of recurrent diarrhea for the past year. On examination, her weight is 10 kg, she was pale, and has a distended abdomen. Laboratory investigations show increased levels of anti-tissue transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA) level. Which of the following should she be advised to eat?

A 3-year-old child presents to the outpatient department with complaints of swelling of the knee joint for 2 days. On examination, his knee is swollen and non-tender with 2-3 bruises over her legs. There is a history of bleeding after circumcision in the newborn period. Which of the following screening test will you perform in this case?

A 3-year-old child presents to the outpatient department with the complaint of tiredness for the past 2 weeks. On examination, his weight is 10 Kg, he is afebrile and pale, and the liver is palpable 2 cm below the costal margin. Complete blood count shows a hemoglobin of 6.8 gm, a total leucocyte count of 4000/m3, a platelet count of 100,000/mm3, and a mean corpuscular volume of 92 fl. The peripheral blood smear shows hypersegmented cells. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this condition?

A 3-year-old child presents to the clinic with coarse facial features and hepatosplenomegaly.  His radiological survey shows, J-shaped sella turcica, immature and ovoid vertebral bodies, the proximal pointing of metacarpals, and bullet-shaped phalanges. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old child with a poor diet presents to the clinic with a complaint of pallor. On examination, anemia is positive with no visceromegaly. Which of the following is the most likely laboratory finding in this child to make a diagnosis?

A 2-year-old girl comes to the emergency department with a history of left-sided weakness for one day. On examination, a systolic murmur was heard at the upper left 3rd intercostal space and it was better heard on the back between the two shoulder blades. She has weak femoral pulses, The dorsalis pedis pulse on both sides is not palpable. The blood pressure in the right arm is greater than in the left arm. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-day-old baby weighing 2 Kg is brought to the clinic with the complaint of jaundice. She has a twin sister who was also delivered 3 days back with her and has no complaints. On examination the baby is plethoric, the respiratory rate is 58 breaths per minute, the liver is palpable 1 cm below the costal margin and the spleen is impalpable. The blood group of the baby is O-positive with a serum bilirubin concentration of 15 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 3-year-old boy presents to the clinic with complaints of bleeding from the nose 2 hours back. There is past history of fever and sore throat 2 weeks back. On examination, he has generalized petechiae, purpura, and bruises all over the body. His heart rate is 110 beats per minute, his respiratory rate is 22 breaths per minute and the child is afebrile. There is no lymphadenopathy or visceromegaly. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 2-year-old child presents in the emergency department with respiratory distress. On examination, the heart rate is 150 beats per minute and the respiratory rate is 60 breaths per minute. Cardiac auscultation reveals a pan systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

A 6-year-old child presents to the clinic with hypertrophy of the calf muscles, associated with difficulty in getting up and climbing the stairs. Which of the following is the most probable diagnosis?
A 5-month-old infant presents to the clinic with a history of multiple brown nodules on his body (café au lait spots) with axillary freckling. He is otherwise normal, what is the probable diagnosis?

An 8-year-old boy with a history of chronic liver disease presents with two massive episodes of hematemesis. Additionally, there is a history of exchange transfusion during neonatal age. On examination, he appears pale and is in shock, with an unrecordable blood pressure. Splenomegaly is noted, but the liver is not palpable. Ascites is also present. What is the most likely diagnosis in this case?

A male child came to the outpatient department complaining of epistaxis and mucosal bleeding. The bleeding time is more than 5 minutes. Factor VIII and VIII C are reduced. There is a history of similar illnesses in the family. What is your diagnosis?
